text: I'm glad we're in a time where endings of anime(MHA, AOT) gets amazing treatment with extended 'Anime Original Scenes' resulting in a reception FAR MORE positive than their Manga counterparts. I remember seeing multiple posts on r/anime after AOT ended trying to explain why the reception was different from the manga. I'm glad these series are getting these top tier treatment from anime staff, that expand upon many things and make smaller changes to make the endings far more satisfying. I always like when Anime expands upon the source material and makes it "better". Idk how it was in the manga for MHA, but I know AOT had some dialogues changes that massively affected how people viewed the ending, not to mention how amazing the final fights are with great music to back it up. text: My Thoughts on Patlabor The Movie This is the second installment in the Patlabor franchise, a sequel to the 1988 OVA, and was written and directed my Mamoru Oshii, who was a decently big anime film director back in the 1980s and 1990s. He's best known for the first Ghost in the Shell movie and its sequel Ghost in the Shell 2: Innocence, but he's also created other works like Angel's Egg, Jin-Roh the Wolf Brigade, and even Urusei Yatsura Movie 2: Beautiful Dreamer. He even did minimal work on anime like Blood the Last Vampire and Blood+, the latter of which was one of my favorite anime as a teenager. If you're in any way familiar with anime history you've probably at least heard his name, but I don't think a lot of people know about some of the popular anim ehe's worked on, even if only in very minor ways. And so because such a legend crafted this movie, there's no wonder that it's better than the OVA that kickstarted this franchise, at least in my opinion. Not tremendously mind you, but I do think it is a little bit. Since it's a movie the animation is obviously better. Not as good as modern anime movies but that should go without saying. The first five minutes of the movie does a great job illustrating how entertaining this film can be at times. And I still think it's the best part of the film, with a close second being the final few minutes, although the bulk of the film still does a decent job with its conversations about war and philosophy and politics, which is what Mamoru Oshii is known for. Although I don't think it's the best he's done, it did come out years before his biggest works either, so he obviously improved as time went on.

text: I watched 'Cowboy Bebop The Movie' without any context I watched the Cowboy Bebop movie, and it served as my introduction to the series. I haven't watched the show yet, so I viewed this purely as a standalone film. I really liked how the world felt like a perfect blend between the normal world and a futuristic one. I didn't experience any confusion while watching it, although I didn’t know the characters' backstories, I didn't have any trouble understanding their personalities. Spike was a very charming protagonist, and Vincent felt like a great villain. They felt like mirrors to each other, I didn't fully grasp it, but that seemed to be what the movie was trying to convey. The opening narration about being alone with no one to play with applied to Spike, and as we learn more about Vincent, we realize it applies to him as well. Even the butterflies that Vincent saw, Spike saw at the end too. ​The villain’s motive was also quite unique, viewing the world as a purgatory from which he wanted liberation. When he met his end, I actually felt a bit sorry for him. The movie was excellent in every aspect, the animation, lighting, colors, and pacing were all fantastic, and the hand to hand combat action scenes were incredibly well choreographed, though I feel like if I had seen the series and known the characters better, I would have enjoyed it even more. While watching, I got a vibe similar to old Hollywood sci-fi action movies, and it definitely felt very Western inspired. Overall, the movie is great, and I had absolutely no trouble understanding the story.

text: Finished Made In Abyss, Heres my thoughts Made In Abyss Review I’ve heard some great things about this show and decided to give it a watch. It exceeded my expectations, the world in itself is incredible. I felt like I was on drugs watching this show, just a super weird anime but extremely fascinating diving into the world. The visuals are beautiful, it's its own kind of anime, never seen anything like it. The anime follows a little girl who's on a journey to find her mother, but in order to do that she has to travel all the way down to the “abyss” which is basically a super large tunnel down, but each layer of this tunnel is like its own world pretty much, dangerous creatures, I loved the adventure theme this anime has, it was a fun watch. Although it follows children, it is much darker than it seems, def has mature themes, with gore and has realism to it for sure, it isn’t softened, you can tell with each layer of the abyss it gets intense and you have to stay on guard or you’ll die, and this anime makes that very clear in very brutal ways. Overall I really really enjoyed this anime, worldbuilding is some of the best in anime, I'd say top 3 easily, I loved the characters, animation and visuals were 10/10, just great anime. I’d put it in my top 6 or 7 now. It's hard to say, prob higher in the future since the story isn’t close to finished yet. Oh and the soundtrack used in this anime is genuinely a 20/10, the music was beautiful, just matched the vibe of the world and made it seem like you were about to watch cinema. 9.5/10
